sourceText: Proof-or-Stop's advanced gates must protect ANY language, not just TypeScript. A py/rs/go bug story must be RED-required exactly like a .ts one — same repro-first required=true flip, same review-assurance-floor material classification — while doc/binary formats stay exempt and this repo's experiments/ scripts stay excluded.
normalizedOutcome: The same type=bug story flips repro-first required=true and classifies material across review-assurance floor + repro classification + ProofStory triggers regardless of source language (.py/.rs/.go/.java/.cpp identical to .ts), driven by one config-resolved, HEAD+materialHash-bound classification snapshot; go.mod at repo root classifies material with no path prefix and no code extension; doc/binary formats stay non-material; experiments/ stays excluded in this repo.
acceptanceClaim: tmp/w1-red/red-language-degradation.cjs exits 0 against the fixed build (all 11 assertions: 5 non-JS sources and 4 cross-ecosystem manifests classify material, 2 doc formats stay non-material), and a no-scope-contract story with one material .go file surfaces exactly one semantic_analysis_unavailable degradation event.
